dialogue.english: Hello, uncle, do you have fresh vegetables?

dialogue.speaker: Vendor
dialogue.arabic: أَهْلًا يَا اِبْنَتِي، كُلُّ شَيْءٍ طَازَج الْيَوْم.
dialogue.transliteration: ahlan yaa ibnatee, kullu shay2in taazaj al-yawm.
dialogue.english: Welcome, my daughter, everything is fresh today.

dialogue.speaker: Vendor

dialogue.english: And how much is the cucumber?

dialogue.speaker: Vendor

dialogue.speaker: Sara

pair.english: This price is a bit expensive.

response.english: I'll lower the price for you.

pair.english: How much are the two kilos together?

lessons.culture: At a market stall you ask the price with بِكَمْ and may bargain a little, and saying الْبَاقِي لَكَ leaves the change as a tip. A polite customer says مِنْ فَضْلِكَ and شُكْرًا with every request.

exercises.tip: أُرِيدُ is 'I want'; add the amount and the thing.

Translate into Fusha: 'Keep the change, thank you.'

exercises.tip: The polite ending مِنْ فَضْلِكَ goes last.

reply.english: Right away, the bread is hot.

reply.english: Yes, open until ten at night.

phrases.arabic: هَلْ تُرِيدُ الْخُبْزَ الْعَرَبِيّ أَمِ الْمَرْقُوق؟

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. هَلِ الْمَخْبَز مَفْتُوح الْآن؟

dialogue.speaker: Hamad

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: أُرِيدُ رَبْطَةَ خُبْزٍ طَازَجَة. بِكَمْ رَبْطَةُ الْخُبْز؟
dialogue.transliteration: ureedu rabtata khubzin taazaja. bikam rabtatu al-khubz?

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: Pita bread, please.

dialogue.speaker: Hamad
dialogue.english: Two riyals. This bread is very hot.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: شُكْرًا. مَرْحَبًا يَا صَالِح، بِكَمْ كِيلُو اللَّحْم الْيَوْم؟
dialogue.transliteration: shukran. marhaban yaa Saali7, bikam keeloo al-la7m al-yawm?
dialogue.english: Thanks. Hello, Saleh, how much is a kilo of meat today?

dialogue.speaker: Saleh
dialogue.english: Sixty riyals.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: أُرِيدُ كِيلُو لَحْم مَفْرُوم وَنِصْفَ كِيلُو كُفْتَة.
dialogue.transliteration: ureedu keeloo la7m mafroom wa nisfa keeloo kufta.
dialogue.english: I want a kilo of ground meat and half a kilo of kofta.

dialogue.speaker: Saleh
dialogue.english: Right away, sir.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: وَأَعْطِنِي كِيلُو لَحْمِ خَرُوفٍ بِدُونِ عَظْم، وَقَطِّعْ لِيَ اللَّحْمَ قِطَعًا صَغِيرَة.
dialogue.transliteration: wa a3tinee keeloo la7mi kharoofin bidooni 3azm, wa qatti3 liya al-la7ma qita3an sagheera.
dialogue.english: And give me a kilo of lamb without bone, and cut the meat into small pieces for me.

dialogue.speaker: Saleh
dialogue.english: As you wish.

response.english: Yes, open until ten at night.

response.english: And you are of the people of goodness.

lessons.culture: Bakeries sell bread by the bundle and butchers sell meat by the kilo, and the butcher cuts the meat the way you ask. Parting words such as بَارَكَ اللَّهُ فِيكَ are a warm way to thank a shopkeeper you see often.

reply.english: Thanks, I hope you like it.

يَجِبُ أَنْ نَغْسِلَ الْأَطْبَاق بَعْدَ ذَلِك

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: What are you going to cook today, mother?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: مَا الْوَصْفَة الَّتِي تُرِيدِين أَنْ تَصْنَعِيهَا؟
dialogue.transliteration: maa al-waSfa allatee tureedeen an tasna3eehaa?
dialogue.english: What's the recipe you want to make?

dialogue.speaker: Huda
dialogue.arabic: وَصْفَةُ جَدَّتِي. يَجِبُ أَنْ نَضَعَ الْأَرُزَّ فِي الْمَاء.
dialogue.transliteration: waSfatu jaddatee. yajibu an nada3a al-aruzza fee al-maa2.
dialogue.english: My grandmother's recipe. We need to put the rice in the water.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Keep the flame low. The food is boiling.

dialogue.speaker: Huda
dialogue.english: Half an hour. Hand me the big spoon.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Here you are. This dish smells delicious.

dialogue.speaker: Huda
dialogue.arabic: الطَّعَام جَاهِز، تَفَضَّلُوا. يَجِبُ أَنْ نَغْسِلَ الْأَطْبَاق بَعْدَ ذَلِك.
dialogue.transliteration: at-ta3aam jaahiz, tafaddaloo. yajibu an naghsila al-atbaaq ba3da thaalik.
dialogue.english: The food is ready, please come. We need to wash the dishes afterward.

response.english: Thanks, I hope you like it.

lessons.culture: When people cook together the cook gives short orders such as أَبْقِ النَّارَ خَفِيفَة, and يَجِبُ أَنْ means 'we need to'. A guest praises the smell of the dish first, and the cook answers with modest thanks.

dialogue.speaker: Reem
dialogue.english: What's your favourite dish, Tariq?

dialogue.speaker: Tariq
dialogue.transliteration: tabaqee al-mufaddal huwa al-kabsa. wa anti?
dialogue.english: My favourite dish is kabsa. And you?

dialogue.speaker: Tariq
dialogue.english: Do you like spicy food?

dialogue.speaker: Reem
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، أُحِبُّهُ. لَكِنِّي لَا أُحِبُّ الطَّمَاطِم النِّيئَة.
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, u7ibbuhu. lakinnee laa u7ibbu at-tamaatim an-nee2a.
dialogue.english: Yes, I like it. But I don't like raw tomatoes.

dialogue.speaker: Tariq
dialogue.transliteration: wa anaa laa u7ibbu at-ta3ma al-7aamid.
dialogue.english: And I don't like sour taste.

dialogue.speaker: Tariq
dialogue.arabic: أُفَضِّلُ الدَّجَاج. وَلَا أُحِبُّ رَائِحَةَ السَّمَك.
dialogue.transliteration: ufaddilu ad-dajaaj. wa laa u7ibbu raa2i7ata as-samak.
dialogue.english: I prefer chicken. And I don't like the smell of fish.

dialogue.speaker: Reem
dialogue.arabic: أُفَضِّلُ الطَّعَامَ الْحُلْوَ عَلَى الْمَالِح. أُحِبُّ الْحَلْوَيَاتِ الدِّمَشْقِيَّة.
dialogue.transliteration: ufaddilu at-ta3aama al-7ulwa 3alaa al-maali7. u7ibbu al-7alawiyaati ad-dimashqiyya.
dialogue.english: I prefer sweet food over salty. I love Damascene sweets.

dialogue.speaker: Tariq
dialogue.transliteration: wa anaa u7ibbu tajribata al-atbaaqi al-jadeeda.
dialogue.english: And I love trying new dishes.

dialogue.speaker: Reem
dialogue.english: Do you like this food?

dialogue.speaker: Tariq
dialogue.arabic: لَا يُعْجِبُنِي هَذَا الطَّعَام، وَلَا آكُلُ لَحْمَ الْخِنْزِير.
dialogue.transliteration: laa yu3jibunee haathaa at-ta3aam, wa laa aakulu la7ma al-khinzeer.
dialogue.english: I don't like this food, and I don't eat pork.

pair.english: Do you prefer chicken or meat?

lessons.culture: To refuse a food politely, say لَا يُعْجِبُنِي ('it does not please me') rather than a blunt no. A guest may also say he does not eat a food, as in لَا آكُلُ لَحْمَ الْخِنْزِير, and the host accepts this without offence.

challenge.title: Shopping and cooking
challenge.instructions: Write a short conversation in Fusha in which you buy vegetables and meat at the market, comment on a price, then cook the food with a friend and say what you like and do not like to eat.
required_elements: a greeting and a request for vegetables
a price asked and a remark on it
a cooking step with يَجِبُ أَنْ
a remark on the smell of the food
something you like and something you do not like

dialogue.speaker: Lama
dialogue.english: Hello, do you have fresh vegetables?

dialogue.speaker: Vendor
dialogue.english: Yes, everything is fresh today.

dialogue.speaker: Lama
dialogue.english: I want a kilo of tomatoes. How much is a kilo?

dialogue.speaker: Vendor
dialogue.english: Four riyals.

dialogue.speaker: Lama

dialogue.transliteration: haathaa as-si3r ghaalin qaleelan, wa lakin yakfee hakathaa, shukran.
dialogue.english: This price is a bit expensive, but that's enough like that, thanks.

dialogue.speaker: Lama
dialogue.arabic: يَجِبُ أَنْ نُضِيفَ الثُّوم. رَائِحَةُ الطَّعَام لَذِيذَة.
dialogue.transliteration: yajibu an nudeefa ath-thoom. raa2i7atu at-ta3aam latheetha.
dialogue.english: We need to add garlic. The food smells delicious.

dialogue.speaker: Friend
dialogue.arabic: أُحِبُّ الطَّعَامَ الْحَارّ، وَلَا أُحِبُّ الطَّعْمَ الْحَامِض.
dialogue.transliteration: u7ibbu at-ta3aama al-7aarr, wa laa u7ibbu at-ta3ma al-7aamid.
dialogue.english: I like spicy food, and I don't like sour taste.

dialogue.speaker: Lama
dialogue.english: The food is ready, please come.
